subject: Commercial plan + MAP & EU residency premium — proposed milestones and timelines
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@finbridge.com>
Date: 2025-11-28T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Mutual action plan & commercial rhythm — quick next steps

Anna — great to meet on the call earlier. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a short mutual action plan (MAP) outline and the commercial framing so your procurement and security teams have something to react to. High level: evaluation -> pilot -> canary -> production ramp. We recommend a 12-week evaluation with two milestones tied to pricing and committed throughput:

- Week 0–4: Evaluation (no commit) — hosted API, EU residency option enabled for test data (standard rate).
- Week 5–8: Pilot (1–3 node dedicated equivalent) — optional 3-month credit if you convert to a reserved commit.
- Week 9–12: Commercial ramp to committed usage — discounts kick in at commit thresholds (10M tokens / mo baseline -> tiered discounts at 30M and 100M).

Two commercial constraints you raised: EU data residency premium and cross-region failover. Ballpark guidance: residency premium +15% on unit pricing; active cross-region failover (warm standby) is a separate SKU with a one-time setup fee and a running premium (~+10% on committed unit price when enabled).

I'm attaching a short MAP spreadsheet (FinBridge_MAP_v1.xlsx) with milestone dates and trigger-based pricing rows so you can share with procurement. Suggest next step: confirm evaluation scope and procurement contacts so we can produce a formal commercial term sheet by Dec 5.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]
[Attachment: FinBridge_MAP_v1.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@finbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@finbridge.com>, Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@finbridge.com>
Date: 2025-12-03T11:42:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & commercial rhythm — quick next steps

Thanks Jordan — the MAP looks helpful. A few procurement/security asks upfront:

1) We need EU data residency (data-at-rest in eu-west-1 and processing within EU) for PII/transactional logs — confirm how that maps to the residency premium you mentioned.
2) For failover: our compliance team requires a cross-region failover plan that does not spill data outside EU for primary data — can Redwood support cross-region failover within EU only (eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1) and what is the commercial uplift?
3) Can you provide SOC 2 artifacts and an expected timeline to provide access to logs for an audit?

On commercial timing: we are targeting an internal board approval window by mid-Jan, so we need the term sheet and a clear ramp schedule to align finance. Please include any credits tied to converting the pilot to a committed Reserved plan.

Regards,
Anna
Anna Müller
Head of Platform Engineering, FinBridge
[Attachment requested: SOC2 evidence pack]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@finbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-05T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & commercial rhythm — quick next steps

Anna — thanks, pulling answers together: short version below, longer doc attached.

- EU residency: we can provision customer-dedicated tenancy in eu-west-1 with logs and storage kept in-region. Residency premium for in-region-only persistence and KMS-bound keys is +18% on unit rates (this covers encrypted storage, regional ops, and compliance evidence).
- Cross-region failover (EU-only): supported with an active-warm standby in eu-central-1. Failover is orchestrated within the EU and will not transfer PII outside of EU. Commercial model: one-time failover setup fee (USD 25k) + running premium +10% on committed unit price while standby is maintained. If failover is only used during DR events and not kept warm, we can price it as a lower-cost dry-run option — let us know which approach your compliance prefers.
- SOC2 artifacts: attaching SOC2_summary.pdf and a redaction-friendly evidence index. Full auditor access requires an NDA/attestation; we can push the evidence pack to your security team this week.

Commercial milestones (proposed — details in FinBridge_COMmercial_Proposal_v2.pdf attached):
- Eval (0–4 wks): usage billed at list (EU residency premium applied if you opt in). No commit.
- Pilot (wk5–8): convert to a 3-mo reserved trial with a 20% consumption credit if you sign within 30 days of pilot close.
- Commit (wk9+): commit levels: 10M tokens/mo -> baseline discounts; 30M tokens/mo -> additional -12%; 100M tokens/mo -> + enterprise discounts (TBD).

We can tie an additional accelerated discount (2–5%) to a multi-region (EU+US) commit if you commit to cross-region capacity for DR. If you instead require EU-only failover, the residency premium remains and the cross-region discount is not applicable.

Attaching proposal and SOC summary. Happy to jump on a call with procurement and your security lead — Karthik is copied to answer technical questions about encryption and KV cache residency.

Jordan
[Attachments: FinBridge_COMmercial_Proposal_v2.pdf, SOC2_summary.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@finbridge.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@finbridge.com>
Date: 2025-12-12T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & commercial rhythm — quick next steps

Anna — looping in commercial lead. Two clarifications from our side to make procurement modeling easier:

1) Ramp credits: For pilot -> reserved conversion we will provide a one-time consumption credit equal to 25% of billed usage during pilot (applied against first invoice post-commit). This is contingent on signing a 12-month reserved contract at the agreed tier.
2) Residency/failover pricing: Confirming Jordan's numbers — residency premium 18% (applied to unit list price), failover warm-standby +10% running premium. One-time DR setup fee USD 25k. If FinBridge opts for a multi-region committed reserve (EU + US) we can offset the residency premium by up to 6% through a blended rate.

Next steps: we can generate a term sheet with the exact commit bands and DocuSign package. Jordan — please send the DocuSign as a staged agreement: signature triggers pilot credits and sets the target commit dates.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: commercial_term_sheet_draft.pdf]

Marissa/Jordan — thanks for the proposal. A few procurement/legal items before we can route to board:

- We need the SOC2 detailed evidence index and a means to run a security questionnaire (we will send a OneTrust link).
- Redlines: currency should be EUR for EU-hosted services; include data-processing addendum (DPA) with EU data subject rights and KMS key ownership details.

If you can get a DocuSign version with the pilot credit and the DPA embedded, we can aim to sign by Jan 18 to hit our board window.

Procurement
FinBridge
